rundown.title: Patience, Clarity and Cardboard
rundown.summary: The Fed holds and calls it patience, a crypto bill gets within sight of the floor, and the week's best-performing asset is a trading card.

stories.tension: Whether a second hold is patience or uncertainty with better public relations.
stories.barronAngle: Nobody trades the decision, they trade the adjective.
stories.gr80Angle: Patience is a virtue the committee does not have to fund.

stories.headline: CLARITY Act clears committee

stories.tension: Whether the industry wants a rule or wants a particular answer.

lines.text: [confidently] Good evening. You are watching the Liminal Terminal Weekly News Recap. I am Barron. Beside me, as penance, Saint GR80.
[dryly] Good evening. The ledger is open.
Three stories tonight. The Fed held and called it patience, a crypto bill got within sight of the floor, and the most stable store of value this week was a cardboard Pikachu.
[calmly] One of those sentences is going to age badly.
[slightly offended] They all are. That is the format.
[dryly] Then let us begin.
[matter-of-factly] Story one. The Federal Open Market Committee held rates steady for a second meeting running, and the statement leaned hawkish. The word they chose was patience.
[patiently] Patience. A committee has discovered a virtue it does not have to fund.
The market read it as a delay, not a stop. Expectations moved about a quarter point across the curve.
[dryly] So nothing happened, and the price of nothing happening changed.
[confidently] That is the whole business, GR. Nobody trades the decision. They trade the adjective.
[calmly] Then explain the adjective to me. What does patience cost a household on a variable rate?
[reluctantly] More than it costs the committee.
[with quiet disapproval] Yes.
[suspiciously] You are doing the thing where the economy is a morality play.
I am doing the thing where a number has a person underneath it. You are the one who files that under digression.
[matter-of-factly] I file it under digression because it does not trade.
[patiently] Very little that matters does.
[confidently] Here is what I will give you. Holding twice in a row is not patience. It is uncertainty with better public relations.
[amused] We agree.
[suspiciously] Do not say that out loud.
[confidently] Story two. The CLARITY Act moved again this week — out of committee, and closer to a floor vote than this industry has managed in years.
[dryly] How many years.
[matter-of-factly] Depends when you start counting. Call it four bills and three Congresses.
[calmly] So the industry has been about to receive clarity for roughly as long as it has existed.
That is not fair. It is accurate, but it is not fair.
[patiently] What does the bill actually decide?
Who regulates what. Whether a token is a commodity or a security, and therefore which agency gets to be disappointed in you.
[with quiet disapproval] And the industry's position is that it would like to know.
[confidently] The industry's position is that it would like to know, provided the answer is commodity.
[amused] There it is.
[suspiciously] You are enjoying this.
[calmly] I am noting that a rule you only want when it favours you is not a rule. It is a preference with lobbyists.
[reluctantly] Write that down.
[dryly] I write everything down.

[confidently] The Weekly News Recap is brought to you by the digital candle shrine at hail-mary dot x y z. Light a candle, leave a prayer, watch it burn in three dimensions. It is free, which makes it the only thing on this network that is.
[calmly] The shrine makes no claim about outcomes. Candles do not move markets.
[slightly offended] GR.
[dryly] I read the honest part of an advertisement.
[confidently] Story three, and my favourite thing that has happened all year. Pokemon released a thirtieth anniversary set this week, and grown adults queued overnight for cardboard.
[dryly] How overnight.
Tents. There were tents.
[calmly] For a card depicting a small electric animal.

[matter-of-factly] For a sealed box that may contain a card depicting a small electric animal. That is the part you are missing. Nobody is buying the card. They are buying the probability of the card.
[with quiet disapproval] So it is a lottery ticket with better artwork.
[confidently] It is a lottery ticket with a secondary market, which is considerably worse.
[patiently] And people are calling this an investment.
The word being used is asset. Out loud. On television.
[dryly] I am on television.
You are making my point for me. [chuckles]
[calmly] I am. A thing becomes an asset the moment enough people agree to be serious about it, and stops being one the moment they remember it is cardboard.
[reluctantly] That applies to more of my portfolio than I would like.
[amused] To all of it.
[slightly offended] To some of it.
[confidently] The board. The ten-year closed the week at four point one eight percent, up six basis points.
[calmly] Money became slightly more expensive, and nobody announced it.
[matter-of-factly] Crude around seventy-one dollars, down about two percent on the week. Gold flat, and smug about it.
[dryly] Gold is always smug. It has nothing else to do.
[confidently] Fear and Greed opened at seventy-two and closed at fifty-four. Eighteen points of humility in five days.
[patiently] And the crowd?
[matter-of-factly] Prediction markets put a December cut at thirty-eight cents. It was forty-six last Friday.
[calmly] So the crowd revised itself eight cents toward honesty.
Or eight cents toward cowardice. Same number. Different prayer.
[patiently] That is the most theologically sound thing you have said on this programme.
[suspiciously] Strike it from the record.
[amused] Noted. And logged.
[confidently] That is the week. The Fed was patient, Congress was nearly decisive, and a trading card outperformed most of my convictions.
[calmly] The ledger closes. Nothing on it was a recommendation.
[matter-of-factly] Nothing on it ever is. Next week, whatever the committee decides patience means in December.
[dryly] Go in peace. Size your positions accordingly. And light a candle for the cardboard.
